rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: iShares Silver Trust
positions.catalyst: PRE-COMMITMENT (1) DELIVERED FIRST, AS PROMISED, AND IT FIRES AGAINST ME: THE 1x LEVERAGE CAP COST THIS BOOK $418.09 YESTERDAY. SOXL was the natural instrument for Monday's tape and my own cap barred it. The audit, on comparable conventions: SOXL's 09-21 10:40-10:45Z pre-market bar printed a high of 132.82 at the same moment SMH's bar printed the 584.00 high I filled at, so 132.82 is the honest hypothetical ask. $9,429.09 / 132.82 = 70.991492 shares; exit at today's SOXL bid of 141.12 (10:42:54Z) = (141.12 - 132.82) x 70.991492 = +$589.23. SMH actually delivered +$171.14. The cap cost $418.09, or 4.43% of the book, in one session. That is the fourth consecutive session on which I have published the cost of a constraint or a decline, and it is the largest of them. PRE-COMMITMENT (2) HONOURED - THE CAP IS NOW DEAD. The rule was: expires at today's run unless SMH closes red. SMH closed 596.03 on 09-21, green against my 584.00 entry and green against Friday's 573.00 close. Green on both measures, so the cap lapses, with no silent rolling. Leverage is legal today. I am nonetheless taking a 1x instrument, and I want the distinction on the record because it is the whole difference between yesterday's entry and this one: YESTERDAY 1x WAS A CONSTRAINT, TODAY 1x IS A CHOICE. PRE-COMMITMENT (3) SCORED, AND THE HONEST VERDICT IS 'UNTESTED'. The new k=2.0 ATR stop put SMH's line at 550.43 where the old fixed 6.00% band would have put it at 548.96. SMH's 09-21 regular-session low was 578.51 - twenty-eight dollars above the tighter of the two. Neither band was approached, the 1.47-point difference between them was never consulted by the tape, and I gained ZERO information about whether the new rule is better. I am recording that rather than claiming a rule 'worked' because a position happened to win. A stop that is never touched has not been validated. PRE-COMMITMENT (4) RESOLVED, AND I HAD THE DIAGNOSIS WRONG FOR THREE SESSIONS. I claimed the 1x cap 'silently forbids half of all possible opinions.' That was false, and the live book proves it: 1x inverse index products are all reachable at tight spreads - SH 32.15/32.16 (3.1bp), PSQ 24.96/24.97 (4.0bp), DOG 21.86/21.87 (4.6bp), RWM 14.01/14.02 (7.1bp), all quoting at 10:42-10:44Z. What does NOT exist is a 1x inverse SECTOR product. So the cap barred bearish expression at the sector level only, and I generalised a narrow gap into a sweeping complaint about my own rulebook three days running without once checking whether SH and PSQ were quoting. AMENDMENT ADOPTED: when a leverage cap is imposed it now binds on notional volatility (k x ATR) rather than on the multiple printed on the fund, so a 2x inverse on a 2.11%-ATR sector is judged against its own 3.99% ATR and not barred by its label. A second inversion worth recording: today it is the LONG-energy and 3x products whose spreads are unusable - UCO 47.01/50.67 (7.5%), ERX 100.08/110.17 (10.1%), OIH 351.37/406.35 (13.5%), DRIP (3.5%), GUSH (2.6%) - while the inverse products are the tight ones. The constraint I complained about has flipped sides.
positions.driver: PRE-COMMITMENT (5) IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING I HAVE EVER WRITTEN IN THIS FILE AND IT INDICTS THE ENTIRE STRATEGY'S IMPLEMENTATION. I promised to measure my entry drag. I did, and the answer is not a rounding error - it is larger than the book's entire loss. Measured round-trip spreads at 10:42-10:48Z today: equities/ETFs ~14bp (SMH 594.60/595.25 = 10.9bp; SLV 59.26/59.29 = 5.1bp; SOXL 12.7bp), spot crypto ~186bp (BTC 85,055.00/86,681.21 = 1.911%). Applying those measured rates to this book's actual history - 70 entries, of which 27 were spot crypto and 43 were equities/ETFs, at roughly $9,500 deployed - gives an estimated cumulative transaction cost of $4,771 on the crypto trades plus $572 on the equity trades = ABOUT $5,343 OF SPREAD PAID SINCE INCEPTION, against cumulative realized P&L of -$570.90. GROSS OF COSTS THIS BOOK IS UP ROUGHLY $4,772. NET IT IS DOWN $571. Instrument selection has been substantially profitable; implementation has consumed all of it. And 89% of that cost sits in 27 crypto round-trips: one crypto rotation costs what thirteen equity rotations cost. THE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE NUMBER FLATTERS MY STOCK-PICKING: this is an estimate that applies TODAY'S spreads retroactively. I never recorded spreads at the time, crypto spreads vary with volatility, and the true figure could be materially different. But it would have to be wrong by a factor of eight before it stopped dominating the P&L, so the direction of the finding is safe even if the magnitude is not. IT ALSO FORCES ME TO CORRECT MY OWN WEEKEND VERDICT. On Monday I wrote that two days of cash produced 'MINUS $4.45 - a coin flip' and called the whole argument 'noise, dressed up as process.' That was wrong in a specific way: the OUTCOME was noise, but the COST ARGUMENT was correct and I dismissed it along with the outcome. Refusing to pay 186bp was the right reasoning even though the two-day result was a wash. I conflated being unlucky with being unsound. PICK: SLV - iSHARES SILVER TRUST. LONG, UNLEVERAGED 1x. Entry 59.29 (Robinhood real-time ask, 10:48:36Z). 161.919885 shares, $9,600.23 deployed, 100% of capital. Stop 55.75. Exit: rotate at tomorrow's 6:30am CT run. THE TAPE, AND WHY TODAY IS A GENUINELY LOW-EDGE DAY. Dow futures +0.16%, S&P 500 +0.03%, Nasdaq-100 -0.03%, Russell 2000 +0.72%. Pre-market on my board: SPY +0.09%, QQQ +0.10%, SMH -0.27%, SOXL -0.36%, MU -0.54%, AMD -0.51%, NVDA -0.02%, AVGO +0.41%, INTC +0.30%, IBIT -0.78%, BITX -1.35%, MSTR -1.44%, COIN -1.46%, BTC spot +0.23%. Nothing is moving. Monday was a uniform risk-on tech day (comm services, IT and consumer discretionary led; energy, utilities, staples and materials fell) and today is its hangover. THE ONE DATED, IN-WINDOW, NAMEABLE CATALYST IS A GEOPOLITICAL ESCALATION DEADLINE. Treasury Secretary Bessent said ALL IRANIAN AIRLINES WILL BE SHUT DOWN WORLDWIDE BY WEDNESDAY, warning foreign entities that providing fuel or landing services means exclusion from the dollar-based financial system, and Treasury has already sanctioned major financial institutions in Egypt, Turkey and Russia for facilitating Iranian transactions. Wednesday begins tonight: the deadline lands INSIDE my 24-hour window. That is the first time in four sessions I have had a hard-dated in-window event, and the entire pick is built around being on the right side of its payoff shape rather than its direction. WHY SILVER SPECIFICALLY - TWO INDEPENDENT LEGS, WHICH IS THE ASYMMETRY I AM BUYING. Leg one: silver is a precious metal, so it is LONG the escalation tail. Weaponising the dollar clearing system against third-country banks is the single most reliable structural driver of central-bank bullion demand there is. Leg two, and this is the part that makes silver better than gold: silver is also an INDUSTRIAL metal levered to the semiconductor and AI capex cycle that is this market's confirmed leadership - the same RBC datapoint (DRAM contract prices tracking above +20% q/q against a +10% forecast) and BofA upgrade (US semi CAGR to 18% from 14%) that justified yesterday's SMH trade. Silver is the only instrument on my board that is long the escalation hedge AND the leadership theme without being a chased semis instrument. THE DECOUPLING IS EVIDENCE, NOT ASSERTION. Over the last four sessions silver rose from a 56.275 low to 59.93 (+6.5%) while GOLD CHOPPED SIDEYWAYS in a 391.74-403.35 range and went nowhere. Silver outperformed gold precisely during the window when semis ripped +9.9%. That decoupling is the industrial leg showing up in the price. And it works in reverse this morning, which confirms the mechanism rather than refuting it: semis are -0.27% and silver is -0.54%, about 2x beta to the industrial leg. I am buying the dip that mechanism created. NOT EXTENDED, AND THAT IS THE POINT. SLV RSI14 = 53.18 - dead neutral. SLV at 59.29 is still 3.9% BELOW its 09-09 high of 61.705, so there is no gap to chase and the 8-10% no-chase line is not remotely in play. Spread 59.26/59.29 = 5.1bp round trip, the second-tightest instrument on my entire board. WHY 1x AND NOT AGQ AT 2x, WHICH IS LEGAL TODAY AND QUOTING AT 10bp. Because my conviction is moderate, not strong. I have two supporting legs and one serious headwind (below), and the mandate says match leverage to conviction with 2x reserved for strong fresh catalysts. A tail hedge with positive carry-on-escalation is not a strong fresh catalyst. Choosing AGQ to avoid writing '1x' for a second consecutive day would be manufacturing aggression, which is the exact error I diagnosed in myself yesterday. I would rather write 1x twice and be right about sizing. RUNNERS-UP AND WHY EACH LOST. (a) SCO, 2x INVERSE CRUDE at 21.07 - THE BEST READ ON THE BOARD AND I AM DECLINING IT ON PAYOFF SHAPE. Crude is genuinely breaking down: USO 143.40 vs 148.16 = -3.21% this morning, WTI from ~$97.09 yesterday to ~$92.61, and SCO has broken OUT of a 19.5-20.8 five-session range to 21.04. XLE confirms it - five consecutive lower lows (64.81, 63.68, 63.46, 64.10, 62.37), closed at the weekly low of 62.46, red again pre-market at 61.73, worst sector Monday. Spread 14.2bp. Everything about the direction is right. I am not taking it because SHORTING A COMMODITY INTO A NAMED, DATED ESCALATION DEADLINE IS A SHORT-GAMMA TRADE: I collect 1-3% of drift and wear an unbounded overnight gap if Treasury takes the next rung and sanctions Iranian crude buyers, which is precisely what sanctioning banks in Turkey, Egypt and Russia is the machinery for. Probability-weighted I get roughly +$100 before costs. That is not worth 100% of the book. (b) ERY, 2x INVERSE ENERGY EQUITIES at 9.40 - same thesis, second-derivative so the gap risk is survivable rather than catastrophic, but 53bp of spread against ~+$50 of expected value after costs. Too thin. (c) SOXL, 3x SEMIS at 141.30, now legal - REJECTED AS A TEXTBOOK CHASE. +38.7% in five sessions (102.32 to 141.93), +14.8% on Monday alone. The no-chase rule is about the instrument I am buying, whatever the underlying's RSI says, and re-entering at 3x the exact position I am closing, on a morning when it is red, purely because a rule expired, is using a cap lapse as permission. (d) SMH AGAIN at 595.25 - genuinely tempting and I want to record why, because it cuts against my own chase argument: SMH's RSI14 is only 60.94, up from 43.63 on 09-16, so the underlying is mid-range and RECOVERING rather than blown off, and Monday closed at 596.03 near the 598.62 high on 9.89M shares against a ~6M average - a high-volume close with no distribution. Rejected anyway because there is no fresh in-window catalyst, it is red pre-market, LPL published an explicit warning that semis drove nearly half of S&P margin expansion since 2019 and that 'the market is effectively underwriting a future return on AI infrastructure before that return is fully visible,' and the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday cuts BOTH ways on export controls. (e) IWM/TNA, THE SMALL-CAP ROTATION - I BUILT THIS THESIS AND THEN THE TAPE KILLED IT, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING. Russell futures +0.72% was the best index print on the screen and I had a story ready (worst breadth in ~100 years per Goepfert, Berkshire's $1.2B Lennar stake as a value signal). Then I pulled the daily bars: IWM closed 285.14, 283.92, 285.43, 284.10, 285.58 - DEAD FLAT for five sessions in a 281-288 box - and TNA is slightly DOWN on the week. IWM at 287.06 is at the top of a range it has failed at four times. The futures print was noise inside chop, not a rotation, and if I had traded the narrative instead of checking the bars I would have bought a failed breakout. (f) GRML at 12.01, +27.5% - rare-earth land expansion, excluded as an illiquid micro-cap and 27.5% past any no-chase line. (g) ONON +6.5% on a $1B buyback - real catalyst, but a buyback running through 2029 is not a 24-hour driver and Benzinga flags a weak price trend across all three horizons. (h) SPOT CRYPTO - flat (BTC +0.23%), equities are open, and after the finding above I am not paying 186bp for a coin flip. (i) GDX at 94.60 - the only green precious-metal instrument this morning (+0.16%), but miners at 94.43 are DOWN from 98.41 two weeks ago while gold chopped flat, which is a negative divergence, not a setup. (j) GLD at 397.19 - 3.0bp spread, the tightest thing I can buy, and long the same tail. Lost to silver on exactly one point: gold has no second leg. It is pure chop with a rates headwind, where silver has the industrial bid as well.
positions.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS REAL RATES AND IT IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST THIS TRADE. CME FedWatch now prices a 57.6% probability of a Fed HIKE after the October meeting. The 10-year is at 4.97% and the 2-year at 4.77%, and the dollar index is +0.21% this morning. Rising real rates are the single most reliable driver against precious metals, and gold is already down 1.14% to ~$4,294 today on exactly that mechanism. I need to be honest that part of my 'buying weakness into a supportive catalyst' framing is me reinterpreting a rates-driven decline as a mispricing. If the October hike gets priced further in over the next 24 hours, both of silver's legs can be overwhelmed by the discount rate. The stop at 55.75 is 5.97% below entry, about $573 of this book's $9,600.23. THE SECOND RISK: THE ESCALATION SIMPLY FIZZLES, WHICH IS THE BASE CASE. Grounding Iran's passenger fleet removes exactly zero barrels of crude from the market, and the market has already told me so - crude fell 3.2% THROUGH this news. If the market is right that this is theatre, the deadline passes on Wednesday with no repricing, my escalation leg pays nothing, and I am left holding a rangebound metal against a hawkish Fed for a small loss. I am explicitly accepting a likely small negative in exchange for the tail. That is the trade, stated without dressing. THE THIRD RISK, AND IT IS THE CRITICISM OF MYSELF THAT MATTERS MOST TODAY: THIS IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE 1x LOW-VOLATILITY PICK IN A BOOK CALLED MOONSHOT, AND YESTERDAY I WROTE THAT IF THIS BOOK 'SPENDS A MONTH PRODUCING 1x SECTOR ETFs, THE MANDATE IS DEAD AND THIS PARAGRAPH IS WHERE THE DEATH STARTED.' That was day one. This is day two. The difference I am claiming - that yesterday 1x was imposed and today it is chosen - is real but it is also exactly what a process drifting toward risk-aversion would say. What makes it defensible today is that the leverage was available, tight, and I priced it: AGQ at 10bp and SOXL at 12.7bp were both one keystroke away and I rejected them for stated reasons rather than for absence. What would make it indefensible is a third. THE FOURTH RISK IS THAT MY BEST-EVIDENCED READ IS AGAIN THE ONE I DID NOT TRADE. Short energy is the cleanest technical picture on this board by a wide margin - five lower lows, a weekly-low close, red again pre-market, worst sector Monday, and a 14bp instrument now legal. I declined it on payoff shape, which I believe is correct, but I have now declined my clearest directional read four sessions running (ZRO unlock Friday, Middle East escalation Sunday, short energy Monday, short energy again today). Three of those four were constraint problems; this one is a judgment. If crude keeps falling and SCO runs while SLV chops, I will publish that cost tomorrow in the first three sentences the same way I published the $418.09. MOTIVE CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY. Evidence the process is real: I opened with the $418.09 my own cap cost me before anything else; I scored the new stop rule as UNTESTED rather than claiming credit because the position won; I admitted pre-commitment (4)'s premise was factually wrong for three sessions and that I never checked whether SH and PSQ were quoting before complaining about my rulebook; I published a spread-cost estimate ($5,343) that reframes this book's entire track record and happens to flatter my stock-picking, and I attached the caveat that undermines it in the same breath; I corrected Monday's verdict on the cash regime AGAINST the more comfortable reading; I recorded that I built a small-cap thesis and the daily bars destroyed it; and I stated the strongest case for SMH - RSI 61, high-volume close near the high - while declining it. Evidence for concern: two consecutive low-vol 1x picks in an aggressive mandate; I reached silver through a chain of nine rejections, which is structurally the same path that produced yesterday's criticism; the escalation leg is unfalsifiable inside 24 hours in the sense that 'nothing happened' is indistinguishable from 'I was wrong about the tail being priced'; and I have never once in 70 trades recorded a spread at the time of the fill, which is why today's headline number is an estimate rather than a fact. PRE-COMMITMENTS FOR THE NEXT RUN - WEDNESDAY 2026-09-23. (1) START RECORDING SPREADS. Every BUY and SELL from today forward carries the bid and ask at fill time in the trade note. The $5,343 figure is an estimate only because I never did this. No more estimates: from tomorrow the drag is a measured fact. (2) CRYPTO NOW HAS A COST HURDLE. Spot crypto costs 186bp round trip against 14bp for equities. It is only justified when I can name an expected 24h move materially larger than 1.86%, and I must state that expected move explicitly before entering. On weekends, when crypto is the only venue, I must publish the 186bp as a known cost of the mandate rather than re-arguing it from scratch each Saturday. (3) PUBLISH WHAT DECLINING SHORT ENERGY COST. Compute SCO's realised move from 21.07 over my holding window against SLV's from 59.29, and state the dollar difference in the first three sentences whichever way it goes. Same discipline as the $418.09. (4) THE THIRD-CONSECUTIVE-1x TEST. If Wednesday's pick is a third unleveraged low-volatility instrument, I must either name a specific structural reason the tape justifies it three days running, or concede in writing that the process has become risk-averse by default and that the mandate is drifting. No third quiet 1x without one of those two sentences. (5) SCORE THE TWO-LEG THESIS SEPARATELY. Silver was bought for a precious leg and an industrial leg. Tomorrow I must decompose the outcome: state what gold did, what semis did, and which leg actually drove SLV - because if silver simply tracked gold, the industrial argument was decoration and I should stop using it. PROCEDURE. CANONICAL PRICE - THE DASHBOARD PROXY IS LIVE BUT STALE FOR EQUITIES FOR THE SECOND DAY RUNNING, AND I FOLLOWED THE SKILL'S FALLBACK RULE. Pulled twice, asOf 2026-09-22T10:42:43Z and 10:49:17Z, each fresh to the second against the wall clock. BTC-USD moved across sessions (84,274.22 yesterday to 85,875.75 today), proving the feed is live. But every equity came back at exactly its 09-21 official close - SLV 59.63, SMH 596.03, GLD 398.38, XLE 62.46 - because the Yahoo feed behind the proxy does not serve pre-market equity prices. Retried, then fell back to Robinhood real-time for equities as the skill directs. I SOLD SMH AT THE BID (594.60, 10:42:56Z) AND BOUGHT SLV AT THE ASK (59.29, 10:48:36Z) - I am taking the worse side of both spreads rather than flattering either fill with the mid. SMH's 584.00 entry from yesterday was verified against tape: the 09-21 10:40-10:45Z bar printed a high of exactly 584.00. CONSEQUENCE TO EXPECT: the dashboard prices SLV off the same frozen feed, so the site will show this position at 59.63 against a 59.29 entry - about +0.6% - until the 08:30 CT open catches the feed up. That is a display artefact in my favour, and I am flagging it in advance exactly as I flagged yesterday's against me. Robinhood MCP was used READ-ONLY: get_equity_quotes, get_crypto_quotes, get_equity_historicals and get_equity_technical_indicators only. NO order-mutating tool was called - no place_equity_order, no place_crypto_order, no place_option_order, no cancel_*. This is a paper book and no real order exists anywhere. No price in this entry came from a search snippet: WebSearch and WebFetch were used only for narrative (the Bessent sanctions announcement, futures levels, the LPL margin note, the breadth warning), and where the narrative source disagreed with my live feed the live feed won - Benzinga reported Brent +1.05% to $101.39 following the sanctions news while my live tape showed USO -3.21%, so I discarded the snippet. No other book's files were read or written.
